skills.title: Skills & courses
skills.description: What a mission asks of the people carrying it. InfoKit writes the vocabulary the whole network shares; your association adds what is genuinely its own.
skills.tabs.label: Skills sections
skills.disabled: Skills and courses are not enabled on this instance.
skills.readonly: You can read these but only a platform maintainer or your association’s admin can change them.
skills.duplicate: That name or code is already taken in this scope.
skills.declarationsHint: People who hold it, plus the requirement sets asking for it.
skills.codeHint: Stable identifier, e.g. permit-b. Lowercase, no spaces.
skills.validityMonthsHint: Leave blank when it never expires.
skills.verificationRequiredHint: On for a driving permit or a certificate; off for a language or a way of working — there, the person’s own word stands.
skills.referenceUrlHint: Where to read about it. A link, never an attachment.
skills.global.title: General skills
skills.global.note: InfoKit writes these once for the whole network — driving permits, first aid, the software several associations share. Every association reads them, and so do the translators working from outside.
skills.global.newHint: A skill every association and translator reads the same way.
skills.ours.title: Our skills
skills.ours.note: What is genuinely your association’s: your own tool, your own way of working.
skills.ours.scopeNudge: If people from outside your association have to hold this — a translator, a partner’s volunteer — set “Read by” to associations and translators. If everyone would write the same row, ask InfoKit to make it a platform skill instead.
skills.ours.newHint: A skill your association asks for and nobody else defines.
skills.promoteHint: It becomes a platform skill: the whole network reads it, and it stops being yours to edit. Nobody’s declaration is lost.
skills.languages.title: Languages
skills.languages.note: Two different questions. A language is a “site language” when content can be published in it, and that is not the same as somebody speaking it: a member may welcome people in Italian on a site that stays unreadable in Italian. So the whole list is offered when someone fills in their profile, and a requirement may ask for any of it.
skills.languages.name: Language
skills.languages.speakersHint: Members and translators who declared it.
skills.courses.title: Courses
skills.courses.note: Training somebody has done. A course belongs to whoever runs it — InfoKit for the ones the whole network sends people to, your association for its own — and “Read by” says how far it reaches.
skills.courses.newHint: A training your association runs, or one InfoKit should hold for everybody.
skills.requirements.title: Requirements
skills.requirements.readonly: Only a coordinator or team lead can write requirement sets.
skills.requirements.newHint: Name the kind of mission, then add its conditions one by one.
skills.requirements.name: Name
skills.requirements.addItemHint: Pick from the skills, courses and languages you can reach.
skills.requirements.mustBeVerified: A verifier has to have confirmed it
skills.requirements.mustBeCurrent: It has to still be valid
skills.requirements.minimumCountHint: Blank means everyone assigned. Two, for “two drivers”.
skills.verify.title: To verify
skills.verify.note: Declarations that asked for a confirmation. Nothing here is a document: you are recording that you know this to be true — no licence number, no scan.
skills.verify.readonly: Only a verifier can decide these.
